data.title: Tether Says It Froze More Than $7 Billion in Illicit USDT and Reissued $1.28 Billion to Law Enforcement and Victims
data.description: Tether said it has frozen more than $7 billion in USDT linked to illicit activity and reissued $1.28 billion to law enforcement agencies and victims. According to Odaily, blockchain analytics firm BitOK examined USDT freezes on Ethereum and Tron from May 2024 to May 2026, finding about $1.89 billion in frozen tokens. On Ethereum, 19% of the $481.6 million frozen in the first year was later unfrozen, compared with 1.2% of the $403.2 million frozen in the second year. Of the USDT frozen on Tron before May 2024, 94% remained frozen as of May 2026. The study counted only amounts that were unfrozen; Tether can also burn frozen tokens and reissue them.

data.title: U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Could Lock 300,000 BTC for 20 Years, but Has Limited Scope
data.description: A proposed U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill could lock 300,000 BTC for 20 years, while limiting the reserve to bitcoin seized by the federal government. According to PANews, the House Financial Services Committee submitted an amendment to H.R. 8957 that removes a provision allowing the use of Federal Reserve resources to buy bitcoin and bars purchases funded by borrowing or tax increases. The amendment would place federally seized bitcoin in centralized custody and lock it for 20 years in principle. Market expectations are that the bill has little chance of being enacted by the end of the year.

data.title: Jefferies’ Mohit Kumar Sees Fed’s December Meeting as Market Turning Point
data.description: Jefferies chief European economist and strategist Mohit Kumar said the Federal Reserve’s December policy meeting may mark the peak in hawkishness and a turning point for markets, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Benjamin Cowen Says Gold and Silver Signal Bitcoin’s Next Move
data.description: Benjamin Cowen says gold and silver typically bottom before Bitcoin, making precious metals a signal for BTC’s next move. Bitcoin may need more time to find a floor while all three assets remain under pressure, according to BeInCrypto. Cowen said the pattern appeared in 2018 and 2022, when metals bottomed weeks or months before Bitcoin. Bitcoin was near $61,500, down more than 50% from its October 2025 record and about 30% this year; gold was near $3,650 per ounce, down roughly 18% year to date, and silver was near $44.20, down about 40%. TedPillows highlighted synchronized Q4 2026 weakness: a hypothetical $10,000 investment at the quarter’s start would be worth $7,147 in Bitcoin, $8,577 in gold and $6,786 in silver. If metals continue falling, Bitcoin could test its realized price near $53,000 to $54,000 or the balance price in the high $30,000s. Cowen sees a stronger recovery as possible after metals stabilize; a durable bottom could make the 2027 outlook constructive. Mike McGlone described a broader unwind across commodities and crypto, while Jared Tate said derivatives and ETFs have made BTC behave more like gold and silver.

data.title: LambdaClass Tests Four Ethereum Post-Quantum Signature Schemes, Recommends Hegotá Prioritize Authorization
data.description:
LambdaClass tested four post-quantum signature schemes for Ethereum and recommended that Hegotá first enable quantum-resistant authorization. According to Foresight News, the ethrex execution-layer client team compared options for native post-quantum signatures in the Hegotá hard fork, which is scheduled after Glamsterdam.

The team said bogota-devnet-2 already includes EIP-8141 (frame transactions), EIP-8298 (SETCODEFROM) and EIP-8151, which could let existing accounts migrate to quantum-resistant authorization without changing addresses. The main missing component is leanSPHINCS, a stateless hash-based signature scheme based on SPHINCS+ whose final parameters are still under discussion.

LambdaClass implemented two stages of each scheme on ethrex: M1, without signature aggregation, and M2, with aggregation by block builders. Under provisional gas and byte limits, each block could include 270 to 385 quantum-resistant transfers in M1 and 385 to 3,591 in M2. A leanSPHINCS signature is about 7,740 bytes, and the prover can aggregate about 400 signatures per second.

The team said aggregation proof generation is costly and recommended allowing users to migrate to quantum-resistant authorization in Hegotá without waiting for aggregation technology to mature.

data.title: AI | ECB Says Euro-Area Workers Use AI at Rates Similar to US Peers
data.description: Euro-area workers are using artificial intelligence at a rate similar to their US peers, though obstacles remain to realizing more of the technology’s benefits, according to Bloomberg, citing European Central Bank research.

data.title: The New York Times: SBF Prison Interview Documentary to Stream on Amazon November 30
data.description:
A three-part documentary about FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, titled The Boy Who Stole Billions?, is set to stream on Amazon on November 30. According to Foresight News, The New York Times reported that the film centers on video interviews with Bankman-Fried in prison; director Nanette Burstein also interviewed his parents and several former co-defendants who had served prison terms, while former Alameda Research CEO Caroline Ellison declined to participate.

Burstein said she considers Bankman-Fried’s 25-year sentence excessive, citing the repayment of affected users and his investments in companies including Anthropic, which she said were sufficient to cover the losses. In an email from federal prison, Bankman-Fried said he took part to clear his name and hoped the documentary would tell at least part of the truth. He has not watched it.

The Netflix series The Altruists, based on Bankman-Fried and Ellison, was released on November 19.

data.title: Trump Says Putin Can Attend G20 Summit if He Wants, Adds, “I Hope He Comes”
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, U.S. President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was unsure whether Russian President Vladimir Putin would attend next month’s G20 summit in Florida, but that Putin could come if he wanted to, and that Trump hoped he would attend.

Trump said some people would not welcome Putin’s presence at the summit, scheduled for December 14–15, 2026, and he doubted Putin would want to come. Trump made the remarks to reporters at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida.

The G20 leaders’ summit is set to take place at Trump National Doral Miami in Doral, Florida. The Kremlin said Thursday that no decision had been made on Putin’s attendance. Putin has said he would consider attending after consulting with the U.S. president, while taking Russia’s domestic situation into account when deciding whether to travel to the United States.

data.title: DCENT Says Unauthorized App Wallet Transfers May Relate to Legacy Signing Randomness, Plans Phaseout
data.description:
DCENT said unauthorized asset transfers from its app wallet may be related to random-number generation in older transaction-signing software and that it will phase out the app wallet. According to Foresight News, the South Korean hardware wallet maker is investigating whether versions earlier than v8.1.0, released before November 5, 2025, generated signing randomness that could be predicted and potentially put private keys at risk. DCENT said this is a hypothesis consistent with transaction patterns observed so far, not a final conclusion, and the investigation is ongoing.

The company said it has found no cases in which its hardware wallet devices were compromised to transfer assets. In the hardware wallet reports it has reviewed, users had also used the same recovery phrase in the app wallet, causing the two wallets to share addresses and private keys. DCENT advised users who reused a recovery phrase in the app wallet to create a new hardware wallet with a new recovery phrase and transfer all assets to it.

DCENT plans to focus on its hardware wallet business and discontinue the app wallet in stages. The ability to create new app wallets will end before the end of 2026, while existing users can continue using the app. The company said it will announce the specific shutdown date at least six months in advance.

data.title: JPMorgan: Stock Sell-Off Nears End, Short-Term Rebound Expected; Growth Risks Could Drag Markets to New Lows in 2027
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, JPMorgan strategists said the sharp sell-off in momentum and AI-related stocks was largely over and forecast a short-term market rebound, while warning that slower economic growth could push markets to new lows in 2027.

The team, led by Karam Choudhury, described the outlook as a “three-stage bear market”: the plunge is largely over, a rebound may follow, and markets face the risk of a choppy decline in 2027.

The strategists said a European long-short momentum strategy had fallen 17.2% over 209 trading days, more than during the Russia-Ukraine conflict and close to the scale of the sell-off during the COVID-19 pandemic. Weak market sentiment, favorable seasonal factors and European quantitative macro indicators returning to a recovery range support a tactical rebound, they said. JPMorgan favors value and small-cap stocks.

data.title: EU Plans Tens of Billions of Euros in Defense Funding to Reduce Reliance on U.S. Capabilities
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the European Union is preparing a new program of loans and grants worth tens of billions of euros to fill gaps left by U.S. cuts to operational capabilities and reduce Europe’s military dependence on Washington, people familiar with the matter said.

The proposed funding would follow the SAFE program, launched last year with €150 billion ($165 billion) to provide EU member states with low-cost financing for urgent defense needs after decades of insufficient investment. The EU is now focusing on the technology and logistics needed for large-scale conflict as the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump cuts related capabilities deployed in Europe.

The new program’s size has not been determined, and it is expected to begin in the second half of 2027. Funding would include some borrowing and money from the EU’s next seven-year budget. The discussions are at an early stage, and the sources spoke anonymously.

The plan would mark a step in the EU’s efforts to achieve military autonomy amid risks from an increasingly assertive Russia and growing doubts about Washington’s commitment to defending other NATO allies. Its final form will depend on consultations between EU member states and NATO to determine countries’ specific needs. The plan will also consider U.S. military capabilities currently deployed in Europe and those Washington has decided to withdraw.

data.title: Zambia Central Bank Holds Key Rate as Inflation Risks Rise
data.description: Zambia’s central bank kept its key interest rate unchanged as new inflation pressures emerge, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Darkfost: Bitcoin Short-Term Holder MVRV at 0.85 May Signal a Long-Term Bottom
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, crypto analyst Darkfost said Bitcoin’s short-term holder MVRV has fallen to 0.85, nearly matching the level seen at the July low. MVRV measures the unrealized profit or loss of Bitcoin holders. Above 1, holders are, on average, in profit; below 1, they are in loss.

Darkfost said the market has returned to a difficult range for short-term holders, who are carrying considerable losses. Historically, levels like these have often coincided with bottom-forming periods and may present an opportunity for long-term investors.

data.title: Nomura Forecasts 50-Basis-Point RBI Hike in December
data.description: Nomura Holdings economists now expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise interest rates by 50 basis points in December, double their previous forecast, Bloomberg reported. They cited surging food prices that threaten to keep inflation elevated for longer.

data.title: DWF Labs: Bitcoin Lagged Nasdaq by an Average 1.2% in 22 Months When Chips Outperformed After ChatGPT's Launch
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, DWF Labs said that since ChatGPT’s launch, Bitcoin underperformed the Nasdaq by an average of 1.2% during the 22 months when chip stocks outperformed the index. During the 25 months when chip stocks lagged the Nasdaq, Bitcoin outperformed it by an average of 3.6%.

Before ChatGPT’s launch, chip stocks and Bitcoin outperformed the Nasdaq by 3.3% and 3.4%, respectively.

data.title: Trader Aoying: U.S. Parties’ Internal Unity Could Spur a Second AI Rally
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, trader Aoying said a second rally in AI stocks could be near if the two U.S. parties achieve internal unity. Even if it does not develop into a major bull market, he said, a daily-chart-level rebound could occur.

Aoying also said an interest rate hike in December was certain, making subsequent dovish remarks more important; he described that debate as short-lived. He said AI technology stocks were now at more attractive prices after the Jensen Huang incident accelerated a market shakeout.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. Stock Futures Rise Before the Open as Semiconductor Shares Rebound
data.description: According to Jin10, U.S. stock index futures continued to rise in premarket trading, with the Dow up about 1.4%, the S&P 500 up about 2%, and the Nasdaq up nearly 3%. Semiconductor stocks also rose: Nvidia (NVDA.O) gained 4.5%; Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) and Micron Technology (MU.O) rose about 8%; AMD (AMD.O) advanced more than 6%; Intel (INTC.O) gained more than 5%; and Broadcom (AVGO.O) rose more than 4%. Anthropic (ANT.O) gained more than 5%.

data.title: Zhipu Short Liquidated as MiniMax Position Moves Within 4.75% of Liquidation
data.description:
A trader’s Zhipu short position was liquidated as the stock rose, while the trader’s MiniMax short moved closer to its liquidation price. According to BlockBeats On-chain Detection, Hong Kong-listed MiniMax rose 16.02% to HK$109 and Zhipu gained 14.95% to HK$336.80 after the market opened in the afternoon on November 27, according to TradingBeats monitoring.

The trader, whose Hyperliquid address is 0x334a, had the entire Zhipu short liquidated. The position was worth about $17,300, and the trader recorded a closing loss of $1,814. The address still holds a MiniMax short worth about $101,600, opened at an average price of $11.54, with an unrealized loss of about $17,300. A further 4.75% rise would reach its liquidation price of $14.57.

After Zhipu’s contract rebounded to $42.94, long positions showed mixed results. Among four tracked positions larger than $100,000, three traders had combined unrealized gains of about $43,200. The largest position, held by address 0xddb8 and opened at an average price of $105.09, remained down $1.823 million.

data.title: Solana Network's Share of Value Capture Falls to 15%
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing data from Unfolded, applications in the Solana ecosystem capture most of the revenue generated on the network, while the network itself retains a smaller share.

Network fees accounted for nearly half of combined on-chain and application revenue in early 2025. By September 2026, that share had fallen to 15%, with applications capturing about 85%.
